heroHeadline: US UNDER SECRETARY COLBY TO BRIEF ALL 32 NATO AMBASSADORS ON FORCE POSTURE REVIEW IN BRUSSELS THURSDAY (AUG 27); EASTERN ALLIES OFFER TO CUT US BASE COSTS TO DETER WITHDRAWAL (AUG 21); FULL LOYALTY QUESTIONNAIRE TEXT LEAKED (AUG 19)
heroSubtitle: As of August 26, 2026, the NATO-US tracker's dominant story remains the Pentagon's Europe force-posture review and the allied loyalty-questionnaire controversy it has become entangled with. Arab News reported that US Under Secretary of Defense for Policy Elbridge Colby will brief ambassadors from all 32 NATO members at alliance headquarters in Brussels on Thursday, August 27 — the most senior in-person consultation on the review since its July launch — with European diplomats stressing the need to present a united front rather than compete individually for US favor. That meeting follows a Bloomberg report on August 21 that NATO's eastern European members, led by Poland and the Baltic states, are preparing to offer to cover a larger share of the cost of hosting US troops specifically to discourage further withdrawals — a financial concession distinct from the political-loyalty signaling the Pentagon's leaked questionnaire has demanded of allies since mid-August. That questionnaire controversy continued to reverberate through the week: Al Jazeera obtained its full three-page text on August 19, Estonian Parliament Foreign Affairs Chair Mihkelson called it an 'unnecessary stress test' on August 21, and former senior US officials Karlin and Smith publicly argued in Defense One on August 23 that basing the force-posture review on ideological loyalty 'erodes' rather than builds alliance trust. The controversy plays out against a backdrop of continued eastern-flank airspace incidents — Romanian F-16s destroyed an explosive-laden naval drone near the Neptun Deep gas platform on August 20, the second Black Sea drone incident in a week following the August 16 Spanish F/A-18 shootdown near the Moldova border.
